chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: Meeting the Ellington men; Cootie Williams and Johnny Hodges
summary: He was in awe among the all-stars, never met Ellington up close, and later recorded with Hodges, who named A Tiny Bit of Blues for him.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you meet many of the guys at the Metronome all-stars date?
Yeah, very few I didn't know, you know. I had met 'em before; we all knew each other.
No, I don't think so... No, not close up.
You mentioned him as one you remember listening to as a child.

Oh yeah, yeah yeah I was glad to be on the scene, no gettin' around that. Just ~~on to~~ be among them. You know, I was just sittin' around lookin' at everybody [ha ha], in awe, as you might say -- to be a member of that, you know great guys like that...
Wasn't Cootie Williams there, yeah -- Cootie and I were good friends. Then I made -- records with Johnny Hodges --
yeah, he even named a record after me. The little blues thing, "A tiny bit of blues," he called it...
